summary: Gives a one-time interpretation of eligibility rules for the 2020-2021 IETF Nominating Committee, needed because the in-person IETF 107 meeting was cancelled. It affects only the seating of that committee. It was replaced by RFC 9389.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 8788 gives a one-time interpretation of NomCom eligibility after the in-person IETF 107 meeting was cancelled. It says to use the five preceding in-person meetings for the 2020-2021 committee and explicitly does not set a precedent for future committees.

subtitle: A one-time NomCom eligibility interpretation for the 2020-2021 cycle.

tldr.problem: Cancellation of the in-person IETF 107 meeting made it unclear how to apply the NomCom meeting-attendance eligibility rule for the 2020-2021 committee.
tldr.mechanism: For that cycle only, eligibility is based on the five most recent in-person meetings before IETF 107: IETFs 102 through 106.
tldr.outcome: RFC 8788 applied only to the 2020-2021 NomCom and was obsoleted by RFC 9389.

facts.label: Attendance threshold
facts.value: At least 3 of the last 5 in-person meetings

today: RFC 8788 is a Best Current Practice for a one-time interpretation and was obsoleted by RFC 9389.

sections.title: Why Eligibility Needed an Interpretation
sections.content: The 2020-2021 NomCom was to be formed between IETF 107 and IETF 108. IETF 107's in-person meeting was cancelled and converted to a virtual meeting. The existing eligibility rule required attendance at three of the last five IETF meetings, so the cancelled in-person meeting raised a question about which meetings counted.
sections.plainLanguage: The usual attendance rule referred to recent IETF meetings, but IETF 107 had no in-person meeting. The IETF needed to decide how to count meetings for this committee.

sections.title: The Chosen Attendance Rule
sections.content:
The RFC records three interpretations: ignore IETF 107, count virtual attendance only so no one loses eligibility, or count virtual attendance like in-person attendance. The chosen interpretation was to exclude IETF 107 from the eligibility calculation.

For this NomCom, people needed to have attended at least three of the five most recent in-person meetings: IETFs 102, 103, 104, 105, and 106.
sections.plainLanguage: The decision was to leave the cancelled in-person meeting out of the calculation. Eligibility used the five in-person meetings from IETF 102 through IETF 106.

sections.title: A One-Time Rule
sections.content: This interpretation applies only to seating the 2020-2021 NomCom and processes related to NomCom eligibility before IETF 108. It does not apply to future NomComs and does not set a precedent. The RFC says future eligibility questions should be addressed through a proper update to BCP 10. It has no IANA actions and is procedural, with no related security considerations.
sections.plainLanguage: The interpretation was limited to one committee cycle. It was not a new standing rule for future committees.

references.text: Kucherawy, M., Ed., Hinden, R., Ed., and J. Livingood, Ed., "IAB, IESG, IETF Trust, and IETF LLC Selection, Confirmation, and Recall Process: Operation of the IETF Nominating and Recall Committees", BCP 10, RFC 8713, February 2020.
